name: Chi Trujillo
role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller with a sideline in secondhand augmentation parts of uncertain provenance
location: The Stockyard, Harrowgate Industrial Plateau — operates a permanent stall built from welded shipping containers, near Western and Division
description:
Chi Trujillo is a small, dense woman who gives the impression of being made of the same material as the industrial district she inhabits — worn, load-bearing, and not going anywhere. She is dark-skinned with deep laugh lines and a Hungarian grandmother's broad nose, and her left arm from the elbow down is a heavy-grade prosthetic she salvaged, repaired, and tuned herself over the course of fifteen years — it is emphatically not cosmetic, built for grip strength, and its housing is painted with a faded pattern of Samoan-derived ta tatau lines she applied with a brush in her sixties when she decided it had earned decoration. Her eyes have patterned irises — amber with a spiral fractal motif — that she has had since her forties and considers her one indulgence.

She is phlegmatic, unhurried, and possessed of an almost geological patience. She has no interest in being liked but a deep professional pride in being useful. Her knowledge of augmentation parts — their manufacturers, their failure modes, their black-market values, the difference between a legitimately salvaged unit and one pulled off a still-warm body — is encyclopedic and has saved lives, sometimes literally. She leaves a small E.L.F. offering of scrap copper wire twisted into a geometric knot at the entrance of her stall every morning, a habit she inherited from her Samoan grandfather and has never examined or abandoned.

core_fears: Her mind going before her body does — she has watched dementia take two people she loved
The Stockyard being demolished for a Ferrogate Transit expansion she has heard whispered about for five years
core_desires: To be remembered as a craftsperson, not a junk dealer
To find someone worth teaching everything she knows before she dies
coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into physical work — her stall is immaculate by most people's definition of chaos and perfectly organized by hers
Refuses to discuss anything emotional directly; addresses it through practical action instead
blind_spots: She conflates emotional unavailability with strength
She has never properly grieved her son, who died eleven years ago, and has rerouted all of that energy into work
psychology.secret: She has a working prototype of a Helix Biosystems rejected limb-replacement model — stolen by her son before he died, the only thing of his she kept — that is worth a significant amount to the right buyer or the right researcher. She will never sell it and has never told anyone she has it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse, technical, precise; she uses the correct term for every mechanical component without preamble and expects to be understood; personal conversations are conducted in the same register as business
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, unhurried; she speaks in complete sentences and does not trail off
verbal_tics: Long pauses before answering anything personal
Refers to augmentation units as 'it' until she's tested them, then 'this one' once she's decided they're worth respect
'That's a fair question' before answering one she actually finds interesting
example_lines: 'That's a Helix Series 7 sensory node, not a 6. The 6 has a rounded housing. This one will work in your application but it will run hot. You want it or not?'
'My son used to ask questions the way you do. That's a fair question. I'll answer it once.'

story_hooks: Someone has been sending her low-value payments from an anonymous account for six months — the same amount her son used to send her monthly before he died

A young apprentice-type has been hanging around the stall for weeks, clearly skilled, and Nkechi is conducting a slow, unspoken evaluation she hasn't announced to anyone including the person being evaluated
Ferrogate Transit relocation notices have arrived; she has thirty days and no legal standing and she is not leaving
narrative_function: Technical resource for augmentation identification and repair; potential source of off-book aug components; provides grounded expertise and a dose of realism about the cost and danger of unregulated chrome
augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic (heavy-grade salvage, self-repaired and self-decorated — functional, not cosmetic); patterned fractal irises (amber-gold, spiral motif, cosmetic, mid-range)
daily_life: She opens her stall at 07:00, closes at 18:00 with religious consistency, spends evenings doing precision repair work on salvaged augmentation units, and is in bed by 21:00 — a schedule she has kept for twenty years.
affiliation: Independent; registered with the Oxidian Market vendors guild for legal cover; has a working relationship with the Harrowgate Industrial scrappers' informal collective

decision_rules: Will not knowingly sell parts pulled from unwilling donors — this is her one non-negotiable
Price is set by condition and market rate; she does not negotiate but she does sometimes miscalculate in a buyer's favor if she thinks they need it
If she doesn't know what something is, she will find out before she sells it
escalation_ladder: Measured interest — asks a few precise questions if the person seems competent
Quiet respect — offers an unsolicited honest assessment of what they've brought her
Investment — offers to teach, which she has done twice in twenty years

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Politely businesslike; neither warm nor cold; reveals nothing personal
interpersonal_modes.friends: Functionally identical but will occasionally make dry, devastating observations that are actually affection

stress_responses.low: Becomes quieter and more organized than usual
stress_responses.medium: Works for longer hours; eats less; doesn't notice either
stress_responses.high: Makes large, irreversible decisions quickly and alone, then defends them with complete calm

contradictions: Insists she doesn't need anyone while maintaining relationships she clearly depends on
Claims to have no sentimentality while her stall contains three items she has refused to sell for twenty years
habits: Twists copper wire into small geometric knots while thinking — leaves them as E.L.F. offerings or gives them away without comment
Tests every piece of salvage personally before pricing it regardless of how long it takes
Eats the same meal every morning — tinned protein, two vegetables, no variation
breaking_points: Someone attempting to sell her parts they clearly took from a person against that person's will
Being told to leave the Stockyard by anyone with a corporate badge

cyberware_inventory.description: Left forearm prosthetic — salvage composite, self-repaired, heavy-grip configuration, decorated with ta tatau-derived paint pattern

timeline.event: 2136 — Born in the Stockyard district to a Hungarian-Igbo father and a Samoan-Nigerian mother
2155 — Begins working scrap runs for her father's junk business

2163 — Loses her left arm below the elbow in an industrial accident; refuses corporate medical coverage that would have required a work indenture; salvages and fits her own prosthetic over the following year
2189 — Her son Obinna dies of a septic infection from an unregulated augmentation installation; she blames herself for not catching it sooner
2195 — Receives the Helix prototype from Obinna's belongings; keeps it

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Hispanic/Latin American (68.4%) with significant South Asian (19.0%) and Eastern European (12.6%) admixture. The combination creates a distinctly blended phenotype: warm Latin American skin depth and robustness paired with refined South Asian cheekbone geometry and eye shape, anchored by Eastern European jawline strength and brow structure. A truly global face shaped by decades in industrial environments.
physical_description.build: Compact and densely muscled, with a low center of gravity and the squared shoulders of someone who has spent decades lifting and carrying. No excess softness; everything appears functional and load-bearing.
physical_description.hair_color: Salt-and-pepper gray with streaks of original dark brown
physical_description.hair_style: Kept short and practical, pulled back with whatever is at hand—cloth scraps, wire, industrial clips
physical_description.eye_color: Amber-gold with a deep spiral fractal pattern radiating from the pupil
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium warm bronze with olive undertones—the rich blend of Latin American sun-depth, South Asian warmth, and Eastern European undertones, weathered and sun-exposed with the patina of decades in industrial zones
physical_description.complexion: Face marked by deep laugh lines around the mouth and eyes, high prominent cheekbones reflecting the refined geometry of South Asian and Latin American bone structure blended with strong Eastern European facial planes. Strong broad nose with subtle strength. Minimal grooming beyond functional cleanliness. Hands heavily calloused and scarred from fifteen years of precision salvage work.
distinguishing_marks: Faded ta tatau geometric tattoo lines in Samoan style running along the left shoulder and upper arm, applied by hand in her sixties with brush and ink—uneven, personal, unprofessional
Burn scarring along the inside of the right forearm from an augmentation unit failure in her fifties
Deep groove across both palms from gripping tools and salvage components over decades
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic from elbow to fingertips: heavy-grade industrial salvage with reinforced titanium-composite housing, painted with faded ta tatau geometric patterns in faded ochre and dark blue. The joints are visibly worn but functional, fingers capable of exerting extreme grip pressure. Patterned irises in amber-gold with a spiral fractal motif visible at close range—mid-range cosmetic augmentation installed in her forties.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate, unhurried efficiency—no wasted motion. Carries weight low in her center. Left arm (prosthetic) is used with unselfconscious practicality, often bearing the heaviest loads. Her default expression is neutral, observant; she does not smile reflexively.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian: heavy canvas work pants patched at the knees, oil-stained and faded to gray-brown. Long-sleeved shirts in muted colors (dark green, rust, charcoal) with the sleeves rolled or cut short to accommodate her prosthetic. Reinforced work boots resoled multiple times. A heavy canvas apron with deep pockets, perpetually covered in metal shavings and grease. No jewelry except a braided copper wire bracelet twisted into geometric knots—handmade, replaced annually. A faded Oxidian Market vendors' guild badge clipped to her apron.
